firstMessage.content:
How I fixed the "Kaggle error" in ARC-AGI-3 submissions

Notebook link: [HERE]

I was getting a generic "Kaggle error" during submission, without a useful public traceback. After debugging, the issue turned out not to be a single Kaggle platform bug, but a combination of notebook/runtime problems.

What was wrong

In my case, the failing notebook was based on a public reference, but the agent was not fully runtime-safe:

  • the agent implementation was incomplete in some versions;
  • one reference had a missing/invalid agent lifecycle implementation;
  • some code paths could fail before the environment received the first valid action;
  • heavy initialization or search could delay the first move too much;
  • the submission relied on assumptions that worked locally but were fragile in Kaggle rerun mode.

One important thing I checked was that the agent must expose the exact methods expected by the ARC-AGI-3 framework, especially:

choose_action(self, frames, latest_frame)
is_done(self, frames, latest_frame)
and choose_action must return a valid GameAction.

How I fixed it

I changed the debugging process to be incremental instead of trying to submit the full agent immediately.

First, I created a minimal "heartbeat" submission that only performed a quick RESET. The goal was not to score well, but to confirm that:

  • the notebook starts correctly in Kaggle rerun mode;
  • the ARC-AGI-3 framework is installed and copied correctly;
  • the gateway connection works;
  • the agent can make its first move quickly.

After that worked, I moved back to stronger agents, but only used references that were complete at runtime. I validated that the selected notebook had:

  • a valid MyAgent class;
  • choose_action;
  • is_done;
  • no placeholder code;
  • no missing methods used during inference;
  • a proper Kaggle rerun branch using KAGGLE_IS_COMPETITION_RERUN.

I also avoided over-editing the reference agent too early. Some stripped-down "safe" versions ran without errors but scored 0.00, so the better approach was to first reproduce a complete working reference, then tune it later.

Result

After switching to a complete runtime-viable reference and validating the agent structure, the submission no longer failed with the generic Kaggle error and produced a non-zero score.

The main lesson for me was: before optimizing the agent, first make sure the notebook can make a fast first valid move in the Kaggle environment. A tiny heartbeat agent is very useful for separating platform/runtime issues from actual solver quality.
